title: How to check your engine oil level
metaDesc: How to check your engine oil with the dipstick: level ground, engine off, wipe and re-dip, read the marks, and add the right oil a little at a time.
first: Red oil light on while you're driving? Pull over and turn the engine off now. Then check the oil.
Park on level ground and turn the engine off. Your owner's manual says how long to wait.
Pull out the dipstick, wipe it clean, push it all the way back in, then pull it out and read it.
The oil should be between the two marks. If it's at or below the low mark, add a little of the oil your manual lists.
dont: Don't touch hot engine parts, like the radiator hose.
Don't overfill. Add a little at a time and check again.

steps.t: Level ground, engine off. Some manuals say to check after the engine is warm and then wait (one maker says 15 minutes) so the oil drains back down. Your manual gives the time for your car.
It usually has a bright yellow or orange handle. Some newer cars have no dipstick and show the oil level on the dash instead. Your owner's manual says which you have.
Pull the dipstick out, wipe it with a clean cloth, push it all the way back in, then pull it out again. The oil should be between the low and full marks.
Open the oil filler cap on top of the engine (it has an oil can symbol). Use a funnel and add a little of the oil type listed in your manual. Wait a minute, then check again. Wipe up any spills.

steps.h: Oil life is not oil level
steps.t: The oil life percent on the dash counts down to your next oil change. It doesn't tell you how much oil is in the engine. Check the dipstick.

call: If the red oil light stays on after you add oil, or the level was fine, don't drive. Have it towed.

sources.t: Kia owner's manual: Checking the engine oil level
